AFDGSP

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
119 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Rain chances and QPF have increased substantially late tomorrow 
through early Sunday for the eastern 2/3 of our forecast area.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Rain chances increase Saturday and especially Saturday night,
with confidence increasing in beneficial rainfall across portions
of the Piedmont.
2. Much cooler from Tuesday onward, with increasing precipitation
chances during mid-week...including possible mountain frozen
precip... although confidence is low.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Rain chances increase Saturday and especially Saturday
night, with confidence increasing in beneficial rainfall across
portions of the Piedmont.

A dry ridge of high pressure persists cross the region this
afternoon, extending from a 1025+ mb surface high pressure center
that will settle into New England by Saturday morning. Meanwhile,
an area of disturbed weather...somewhat tropical, but mostly
baroclinic in nature continues to impact northern Florida and
areas just off the Southeast Coast. This area will begin to
organize, while kicking out to the northeast as large scale
height falls currently impacting the western Conus will begin
overspreading the eastern half of the country Saturday through
early Sunday. Deterministic and ensemble forecast systems generally
agree in primary surface development occurring off the Southeast
Coast. However, there is a growing consensus that some element
of secondary development/enhanced isentropic lift over the stable
surface wedge will occur inland along the baroclinic zone in the
GA/SC area...suggesting significantly higher rainfall chances and
QPF than previously forecast. PoPs for Sat night have therefore
been increased to at least likely across the eastern half of the
area, with categorical chances roughly along/east of I-77. Rainfall
amounts will mostly be in the 0.1-0.33" range, but 0.5"+ is looking
more likely along/east of I-77.

Max temperatures return to near-normal across much of the area
Saturday under thickening cloud cover. High temps increase a bit
Sunday with rain chances diminishing in the morning, but residual
in-situ cold air damming conditions could persist through at least
part of the day. Monday is forecast to be quite warm...10+ degrees
above climo as skies likely clear and downslope/compressional
warming develops in advance of approaching frontal boundary. This
front could bring some low-impact showers to the mountains Monday
afternoon/evening, but will otherwise be moisture starved by NW
flow/subsidence on the west side of cyclone moving quickly up the
Northeast Coast. Min temps are forecast to be 5+ degrees above
climo through early next week owing to some combination of cloud
cover/elevated dewpoints/overnight mixing.


Key message 2: Much cooler from Tuesday onward, with increasing
precipitation chances during mid-week...including possible mountain
frozen precip... although confidence is low.

Height falls and an attendant, mostly dry cold front cross the
region Monday night/early Tue, bringing much cooler temperatures,
which are forecast to be near-to-below normal from Tue through
the end of the week. Otherwise, the global forecast models suggest
low forecast confidence from around mid-week onward, as a highly
amplified and rather complex upper air pattern evolves over the
Conus, with little intra-model agreement regarding the short wave
details. There is a developing, albeit still-weak consensus of
development of Miller-B cyclone scenario during mid-week, although
there is no consensus regarding the timing of associated precip
chances for our forecast area. There is enough of a signal in
guidance to feature mostly chance PoPs from Wed through at least
the first part of Thanksgiving Day. Depending upon timing, enough
cold air could be in place over the mountains to support some
transient period of wintry precip at the onset of any precip event.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: VFR conditions are forecast to prevail
through this TAF period, with slowly increasing/lowering mid and
high level clouds expected, especially from later this afternoon
through tonight. Chances for rain will gradually increase from
the south through the daylight hours Saturday, although holding
off until later in the afternoon for the TAF sites. NE winds will
generally favor speeds of around 10 kts (except for more light/vrbl
conditions at KAVL), with gusts of around 20 kts becoming possible
late tonight into Saturday.

Outlook: Chances for rain and associated restrictions continue to
increase late Saturday into early Sunday...mainly for terminals east
of the mountains. Restrictions could linger well into Sunday. A
cold front may bring rain chances back along the NC/TN border
Monday before better rain chances, and possible restrictions,
return area-wide by mid-week.
